previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and recent DVT/PE on anticoagulation was admitted for bilateral lower extremity pain and severe calf cramping. Evaluation revealed stable clot burden on ultrasound with partial clearance in the greater saphenous vein and no new DVT. Ankle X-rays showed no fractures or avascular necrosis. The pain was attributed to a combination of radicular nerve symptoms from prior back surgery and possible joint-related discomfort. He was managed with gabapentin for neuropathic pain, acetaminophen, and PRN opioids. His chronic conditions remained stable, and he was discharged home with instructions to hold warfarin on the day of discharge, restart the next day, follow up with primary care and podiatry, and monitor weight for signs of fluid retention.
problems: Pain in joint, ankle and foot
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of deep vessels of proximal lower extremity
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  History of PE, now with chest pain similar to the prior presentation
for PE.  Evaluate for acute pulmonary embolus.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained from the suprasternal
notch to the upper abdomen without contrast and low-dose radiation at first,
followed by an early arterial phase scanning after the administration of 100
cc of Omnipaque.  Multiplanar reformatted images in coronal and sagittal axes
were generated.  Oblique MIPs were prepared in an independent workstation.

DLP:  389.36 mGy-cm. 

COMPARISON:  CTA chest from ___.

FINDINGS:

CT thorax:  The aorta and main thoracic vessels are well opacified.  The aorta
demonstrates normal caliber throughout the thorax without intramural hematoma
or dissection.  There is atherosclerotic disease without aneurysm.  The
pulmonary arteries are opacified to the segmental level.  There are tiny
partially occlusive filling defects within the bilateral pulmonary arteries,
which represent resolving pulmonary emboli.  The clot burden is decreased from
___.  There is no evidence of an acute pulmonary embolus.  No
arteriovenous malformation is seen. 

Motion limits evaluation of the lower lungs.  The airways are patent to the
subsegmental level and there are mild emphysematous changes.  The patient is
status post coronary stent placement.  The heart, pericardium, and great
vessels are otherwise unremarkable.  There is no focal consolidation, pleural
effusion, or pneumothorax. 

Osseous structures:  No focal osseous lesion concerning for malignancy. 

Although this study is not designed for the assessment of intra-abdominal
structures, the visualized solid organs and the stomach are unremarkable.  

IMPRESSION:

Minimal partially occlusive filling defects, representing resolving pulmonary
emboli.  No evidence of acute PE.  

The revised findings were discussed via telephone by Dr. ___ with
Dr. ___.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Chest pain, recent PE.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest are provided.  The lung volumes
are low with bronchovascular crowding and atelectasis noted in the lower
lungs.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable.  No convincing signs of
pneumonia, effusion or pneumothorax.  Bony structures appear intact.

IMPRESSION:  Limited, negative.  Please refer to subsequent CTA chest for
further details.
